title: Six Winters and One Short Note
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事）　|　核心词汇：feeling　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 feeling 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 my aunt ① had a feeling that no doctor in the clinic would have named, and she said the having was the whole of the winter. The ② feeling, meaning the sense itself and not the pain, ran six winters and stayed unnamed in the book; a feeling, she said, is the only thing in a clinic that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ feeling in that clinic had the same short note beside it, and the ④ feeling at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the night and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A feeling, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; my aunt said the naming is the part that fills six winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the feeling was the whole of the room, meaning the mood and not the sense. The ⑥ feeling, meaning the mood and not any of that, is the only thing in a room that everybody waits for and nobody names; feeling, he said, is either something you have or the only word that means both a sense and a mood. He said the mood is the part they remember.

By 1961 the ⑦ feeling had become a line in a card, and the card had become an argument about the short note. The ⑧ feeling of the whole thing, my aunt wrote in January, was one clinic and six winters of naming; feeling, she said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to name. She said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ feeling I remember is the one named in the card, which closed in 1963 and is still described as the quietest in the clinic. A ⑩ feeling, my mother said in 1965, is the only one that improves by being named; every feeling, she said, is a mood that has agreed to look like a sense. She said the mood was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 感觉；感受（指诊所里每一种旁边的那一种）
B. n. 感觉（指那一种本身，与疼痛相对）
C. 固定搭配：have a feeling 有一种感觉
D. n. 感觉（指留给夜晚的那一种）
E. n. 感觉（抽象总称，指一间诊所的感受之事）
F. n. 感觉（指卡片上写到、被说出的那一种）
G. n. 气氛；情绪（指一间屋子里人人都等却无人说出的那样东西）
H. n. 气氛（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说出的那样东西）

items.q: had a feeling that no doctor in the clinic would have named
The feeling, meaning the sense itself and not the pain
the feeling at the far side
the feeling was the whole of the room
the feeling had become a line in a card
The feeling of the whole thing
A feeling, my mother said in 1965

answers.why: have a feeling 意为“有一种感觉”，1955 年姑姑有一种诊所里没有一位医生肯说出的感觉。
feeling 意为“感觉”，指那一种本身而不是疼痛，它经过了六个冬天而在簿子上没有名字。
feeling 意为“感觉”，指诊所里每一种旁边的那一种，每一种旁边都有同一张短短的字条。
feeling 意为“感觉”，指留给夜晚的那一种，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
feeling 意为“气氛、情绪”，指一间屋子里人人都等却无人说出的那样东西，叔叔说这份气氛就是那间屋子的全部。
feeling 意为“气氛”，指人人都等却无人说出的那样东西而不是那一种感觉，是屋子里人人都等、却无人说出的东西。
feeling 意为“感觉”，指卡片上写到、被说出的那一种，到 1961 年这一种成了卡片里的一行。
feeling 意为“感觉”，姑姑一月写道，整件事的感受之事是一间诊所和六个冬天的说出。
feeling 意为“感觉”，我记得的是卡片上说出的那一种，1963 年结束了，至今仍被说成诊所里最安静的一种。
feeling 为抽象总称，母亲 1965 年说，一种感觉是唯一会因为被好好说出而变得更好的东西。
